source_refs.note: Exercise 14.4 Q3, book p.290 (PDF 295). No key answer (proof); determinant = 0 and c = 3a + b (sympy). Solution book PDF 1271 agrees.

blocks.prompt: 3 Prove that the vectors \(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(-2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) and \(\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) are coplanar.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh coplanar (ek hi plane mein hone) ka proof hai.
Diya kya hai? Teen vectors.
Saabit kya karna hai? Ke teeno ek hi plane (satah) mein parre hain.
Rule kaunsa? Teen vectors tabhi coplanar hote hain jab un ka scalar triple product 0 ho (14.4.5).
Plan: components ka determinant bana kar dikhana ke us ki value 0 hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\underline{a} = \underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = -2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\), \(\underline{c} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\).
Humein saabit karna hai: \(\underline{a}, \underline{b}, \underline{c}\) coplanar hain.
Tareeqa: \([\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}]\) un vectors par bane parallelepiped ka volume hai. Agar teeno ek hi plane mein hon to dabba bilkul chapta (flat) ho jata hai, jaise kaagaz, aur us ka volume 0 hota hai. Ulta bhi sahi hai: volume 0 ho to vectors coplanar hain. Is liye bas determinant 0 dikhana hai.

Determinant likhein
\[[\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}] = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & -3 & 5 \end{vmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har row ek vector ke components hain, \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) ki tarteeb mein.

Row 1 se expand karein
\[= 1(15 - 12) + 2(-10 + 4) + 3(6 - 3)\]
\[= 3 - 12 + 9 = 0\]
Kyun: Pehla minor \((3)(5) - (-4)(-3) = 15 - 12 = 3\). Doosra minor \((-2)(5) - (-4)(1) = -10 + 4 = -6\); is ke saath sign minus hai aur entry khud \(-2\) hai, to \(-(-2) = +2\) bana. Teesra minor \((-2)(-3) - (3)(1) = 6 - 3 = 3\).
Dhyan dein: \((-4)(-3)\) positive 12 hai; isay minus samajhna aam ghalti hai.

Nateeja aur tasdeeq
\[\underline{c} = 3\underline{a} + \underline{b}\]
\[3\underline{a} + \underline{b} = (3 - 2)\underline{i} + (-6 + 3)\underline{j} + (9 - 4)\underline{k}\]
\[= \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Triple product 0 aaya, is liye vectors coplanar hain. Tasdeeq ke liye dekha ke \(\underline{c}\) asal mein \(\underline{a}\) aur \(\underline{b}\) ka mel hai; jo vector do vectors ko jor kar ban jaye woh unhi ke plane mein rehta hai. Yeh khud sochne ki baat hai: plane ke andar chalte rahein to bahar nahi nikal sakte.
blocks.final_answer: \([\underline{a}\ \underline{b}\ \underline{c}] = 0\). Saabit ho gaya: teeno vectors coplanar hain.
